texts: Keepers extinguish the lantern at dawn with a brass snuffer.
Keepers often inherit the snuffer with the station.

fields.sentence: Keepers extinguish the lantern at dawn with a brass snuffer.
parse: (: keeper_extinguish_rule (Implication (Member $x keeper) (And (Member (sk_extinguish $x) extinguish) (Agent (sk_extinguish $x) $x) (Patient (sk_extinguish $x) sk_lantern_1) (Time (sk_extinguish $x) dawn) (Instrument (sk_extinguish $x) (sk_snuffer $x)) (Member (sk_snuffer $x) brass_snuffer))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: Bare-plural generic at 0.9/0.9 with no companion (no quantifier word), the indefinite snuffer as a dependent Skolem per keeper, day-part "dawn" as a bare Time symbol, and brass_snuffer fused with the head genus only (a noun modifier is never exposed) all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: Keepers often inherit the snuffer with the station.

q2_gaps: A bound / functional DEFINITE singular inside a generic distributing rule ("Keepers often inherit the snuffer with the station" — each keeper's own snuffer and station): the instruction set's definite rule mints one shared constant witness asserted at top level (as `sk_causeway_1` in "Foxes rarely cross the causeway"), and the Skolem-function machinery is defined only for dependent EXISTENTIALS ("some book"), so a definite that co-varies with the quantified subject has no stated route.
review.notes: The parse's `(sk_snuffer $x)` / `(sk_station $x)` gives the semantically right per-keeper reading, which a shared constant would get wrong, so I read it as faithful despite the unstated route. "often" → strength 0.8 plus the QuantifierPhrase companion, Agent/Theme and the residual `With` oblique are all as specified, and `snuffer` correctly stays a plain kind (referring use of an agent-nominalization).
